newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia pulls last troops from Chechnya - officials.
newsitem.headline: Russia pulls last troops from Chechnya - officials.

text.p: Russia has withdrawn the last of its defence ministry troops from Chechnya, a ministry spokesman said on Sunday in an announcement marking a formal end to Moscow's ill-fated military campaign in the region.

"Today there are no defence ministry troops in Chechnya. They are all withdrawn," said defence ministry spokesman Viktor Tkachenko. The withdrawal of all interior ministry troops from the rebel region had been announced earlier on Sunday.
A different defence ministry official had said earlier on Sunday that some troops remained in the region.
Tkachenko said he did not know exactly when the last defence ministry troops had been pulled out but that they had left before the last interior ministry troops.
Interfax news agency quoted the interior ministry troops' chief of staff, Lieutenant-General Pavel Maslov, as saying all the troops had left the war-torn North Caucasus region.
"I officially announce that as of today not one soldier of the interior ministry or the defence minstry of the Russian Federation remains in Chechnya," it quoted Maslov as saying.

Maslov had told RIA news agency earlier on Sunday that the interior ministry troops had left but did not mention the defence ministry forces. He said contradictory information about the pullout had been spread deliberately "to avoid possible provocations".

President Boris Yeltsin sent the troops to the region in December 1994, starting a bloody and ill-fated 21-month military campaign against separatists. He ordered the gradual withdrawal to pave the way for elections on January 27.
Tens of thousands of people, mostly civilians, were killed in the fighting before the signing of a ceasefire and peace deal on August 31.
